verses.55:35: يُرۡسَلُ عَلَيۡكُمَا شُوَاظࣱ مِّن نَّارࣲ وَنُحَاسࣱ فَلَا تَنتَصِرَانِ

meaning: The root شَوَظَ (shawaẓa) carries a single sense in the classical lexica. Ibn Fāris records it as كلمة واحدة — one word — الشُّوَاظ, flame from a fire unaccompanied by smoke, and cites the Quranic شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ.
en_note: Statistically derived from translation co-occurrence, not a lexical definition. Highlighting only.
meaning_previous: The root شُوَاظٌ (shuwazh) refers to flame without smoke, or the heat of fire or the sun. It can also metaphorically describe intense thirst or clamor.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
